data.title: MSCI India Gets Rare Earnings Upgrade — Market Talk
data.description: Jefferies has raised its earnings forecast for the MSCI India index by about 1%, citing Indian companies' resilient earnings. As a potential slowdown in artificial-intelligence spending threatens earnings in South Korea and Taiwan, India could also benefit from continued foreign portfolio investment flows, Jefferies analysts say in a note. Such an earnings upgrade is rare: forecasts for the index have been cut in 18 of the past 20 fiscal years, the brokerage says. Revenue at the Indian companies it covers grew 21% in the September quarter, the fastest pace in nearly four years, the analysts say. ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, State Bank of India and Reliance Industries are among Jefferies' preferred stocks. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)

data.title: Bitcoin miners log longest block gap since July at 98 minutes
data.description:
Bitcoin is designed to produce a new block roughly every 10 minutes. On November 26, 2026, the network took 98 minutes and 19 seconds.

That gap between blocks 977,697 and 977,698 is the longest since July. Anyone waiting on a confirmation during that window waited a lot longer than usual.

Miners went more than an hour and a half without finding a valid block. Transactions in the queue were stuck for over 90 minutes during the gap.

The last time the network stalled this long was July 6, 2026. Block 956,953 arrived after a 112-minute, 26-second wait, so November's delay is the second longest of the year so far.

Galaxy Research ranks the November gap as the 69th longest since 2011. It is also the third delay of this size in 2026, according to the firm's analysis.

Alex Thorn, who heads Galaxy Research, flagged the event and where it falls in the historical record. His team's data puts gaps of this length at about once every 18,600 block intervals, or roughly once every four months.

The longest verified gap in Bitcoin's history lasted 141 minutes and 1 second, in October 2011. November's 98-minute pause is long, but well short of that record.

The 10-minute block time is an average. It works less like a train schedule and more like waiting for someone to roll a specific number on a die with trillions of sides.

Miners compete by guessing numbers until one of them produces a hash that meets the network's difficulty target. Every guess is independent, so the network has no memory of how long it has already been waiting.

This is known as a Poisson process. In everyday terms, each new minute has the same odds of producing a block as the one before, no matter how long the drought has run.

Bitcoin holds that average in place through difficulty adjustments every 2,016 blocks. If blocks have been coming too slowly, the puzzle gets easier, and if they have been arriving too fast, it gets harder.

A single long gap barely moves that calculation. It is one data point among thousands, so the difficulty does not swing in response to one slow stretch.

For most holders, a 98-minute gap went unnoticed. Coins stayed put, balances did not change, and the ledger's security was not affected.

The people who noticed were those trying to move money. Exchange deposits, merchant payments and transfers between wallets all sat unconfirmed until block 977,698 landed.

Fees behave oddly in this situation. During normal congestion, users can outbid each other to jump the queue, but a block drought removes that option entirely since there is no block space to bid on.

Galaxy Research's view is that gaps like this come from natural variance in mining rather than a malfunction. Nothing in the available data points to an outage, an attack or a problem with the chain itself.

The numbers argue for calm. If gaps of this length show up about once every four months, as Galaxy's data suggests, then three in a single year is roughly what the math would predict.

The more useful thing to watch is the trend in block times across a full difficulty period rather than any single outlier. A sustained slowdown across hundreds of blocks would say something about network conditions, while one 98-minute gap mostly says the dice landed badly for a while.

The 141-minute record from October 2011 has now stood for well over a decade.

data.title: Bangladesh loses half of Adani's Godda power supply
data.description:
Bangladesh will get only half the electricity it normally receives from Adani Power's 1,600-MW coal-fired Godda plant in India's Jharkhand state until December 18, after one of the plant's two units shut for annual maintenance, India Today reported on November 25.

The outage comes as Bangladesh relies more heavily on imported power during a wider energy shortage. The country also faces rising living costs, wage protests by garment workers and political uncertainty ahead of a promised return by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.

The 800-MW unit went offline at about midnight on November 25-26, while the second unit of the same size keeps running as usual. Adani Power described the shutdown as planned and part of its regular upkeep programme, The Business Standard reported. The work covers inspections, servicing and preventive maintenance meant to keep the unit reliable and avoid technical faults.

The Bangladesh Power Development Board approved the shutdown on October 26, according to bdnews24.com. The board signed a 25-year power purchase agreement with Adani Power in 2017 that obliges the plant to deliver 1,496 MW.

Bangladesh imported an average of 46mn units of electricity a day from India in the first half of November. That compares with 33.6mn units in October, even though domestic demand and generation fell as winter set in, bdnews24.com reported.

Unplanned outages have also hit the plant. On September 10, a fault in a boiler feed pump took Unit 2 off the grid, and Adani's supply to Bangladesh dropped to 691.44 MW, down from 1,430.06 MW during the September 9 evening peak. Three days passed before the unit was running again.

That month the power shortfall in Bangladesh hit 3,000-3,500 MW, leaving several districts without electricity for between three and 10 hours daily. In protest, an alliance of 11 parties headed by Jamaat-e-Islami undertook a long march that ran from Dhaka to Chattogram.

According to The Daily Star, the electricity prices Bangladesh charges retail customers went up 16.68% in June. Then, with import costs and global oil prices rising, the government increased what it charges for diesel, petrol and kerosene in September.

Hasina, now living in exile in India, will come back on December 16, according to one of her aides. Members of the Awami League who hid after the uprising are beginning to resurface. There have been reports of clashes involving police, as well as arson attacks targeting police stations, properties tied to the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, and the ancestral house of Muhammad Yunus, who heads the interim government.

data.title: Australia Orders LNG Exporters Reserve Some Gas to Plug Shortages at Home
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australia will require liquefied natural gas exporters to reserve up to a fifth of their shipments for the domestic market to help lower power bills for local households and businesses.

The law, approved early Friday, comes amid forecasts of supply shortfalls along the country's densely populated east coast--including Sydney and Melbourne--as traditional local gas fields deplete. The requirement takes effect Jan. 1, 2028, to align with industry contracting cycles, officials said.

"Australia has abundant gas resources and Australians should benefit from them," said Resources Minister Madeleine King. "This scheme will make more Australian gas available to our households and businesses, putting downward pressure on prices."

Australia is among the world's largest LNG exporters following significant investment by companies such as ConocoPhillips and Shell. The majority of Australian LNG is shipped to Japan, China, and South Korea, with about three-quarters sold under long-term contracts.

Write to Rhiannon Hoyle at rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com

data.title: Philippines' trade deficit widens to $6.9 billion in October
data.description:
The Philippines posted a trade deficit (PHTBAL=ECI) of $6.95 billion, wider than the previous month's trade gap of $5.15 billion, preliminary official data showed on Friday.

Imports (PHIMP=ECI) rose 50.4% in October from a year earlier to $17.5 billion, while exports (PHEXP=ECI) climbed 41.8% to $10.6 billion, the Philippine Statistics Authority said.

data.title: Bank of America sees the S&P 500 climbing to 7,800 next year, making up lost ground
data.description:
The stock market will have to make up some ground in 2027, according to Bank of America.

Savita Subramanian, the firm's head of US equity strategy, expects the S&P 500 will climb to 7,800 by the end of next year. The target implies just an 8.3% climb from Tuesday's close that the strategist said represents a better entry point for investors after this month's corrective action.

It's also a level that the S&P 500 had already reached. The broader index first topped 7,800 in October, before a rapid succession of developments in November — including the exit and then reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, and the Democratic sweep of Congress during the midterm elections — finally cracked a stock market that's been sputtering for roughly half a year.

The strategist expects that the choppy trading action could continue next year, as supply and demand dynamics deteriorate in the market and the question around AI sustainability continues to weigh on investors.

"What keeps us worried?" she wrote Tuesday. "Worsening supply (IPOs/issuance) vs. demand (waning buybacks, aging demographics suggesting risk of retirement fund outflows). Fading earnings/margin visibility and questions around the durability of the AI investment cycle plague us, and high expectations plus, until recently, S&P index complacency ('Don't risk it with single stocks, just buy the index') increase downside risk."

The conflicting cross currents in the market also implies a wide range of outcomes. The strategist expects that the S&P 500 can rise to 8,500 in her bull case, and fall to 6,600 in her bear case.

For the bulls, a neutral sentiment reading in the firm's sell side indicator implies double-digit equity returns. For the bears, a poor reading in the firm's earnings surprise indicator suggests earnings next year could disappoint investors, relative to expectations.

Still, there remain buying opportunities. The strategist highlighted communication services as a buying opportunity, raising the sector to overweight. She also expects AI adopters such as financials and health care will outperform.

One contrarian take she had was a switch to overweight consumer discretionary and underweight staples, thanks to an overdue housing turnover cycle that should mean a rise in discretionary spending as Americans make home purchases.

That could help investors wade through a bull market that's in its fifth year, with gains tougher to come by. Tuesday's trading was also volatile, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite dropping after rallying just the prior day. The broader index closed Tuesday just above 7,200.

data.description: Press Metal Aluminium's longer-term prospects could remain positive, Maybank IB analyst Loh Yan Jin says in a note. data.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer
data.description:
The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade triggers heightened volatility.

The dollar index , which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.81, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently flat.

The US currency edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen early in Friday's Asian session, and also strengthened slightly to 0.83455 Swiss franc .

The euro was little changed at $1.0964 and sterling eased slightly to $1.3099.

The risk-sensitive Aussie dollar weakened a touch to $0.6631, after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

"All eyes are on whether the downtrend in AI-related stocks will turn around," Mizuho analysts wrote in a client note.

A recovery could see currencies such as the Aussie and high-yielding Mexican peso bounce back, while renewed selling would likely see those currencies under additional pressure, they said.

The US currency has been supported by expectations for Federal Reserve policy tightening with traders seeing a quarter-point interest rate hike on December 9 as a near certainty, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Hotter-than-expected US core personal consumption expenditures inflation in October, a sharp upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product and a Federal Reserve survey showing continued economic growth and sticky inflation also have traders confident of an additional hike by around April.

The dollar index has risen about 5.7% so far in 2026, with only a month left in the year.

"The USD looks to be on a stronger-for-longer path than previously expected," NAB strategists wrote in a research report.

However, "given its rapid rise, we see limited scope for further gains," they added.

data.title: Young Thai Speaker Shares Family's Sustainability Story at UN COP31 with 51Talk
data.description:
Bodhi, son of 51Talk Thailand brand ambassador Shahkrit Yamnarm, shares his family's approach to sustainable farming at the UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Türkiye.

ANTALYA, Türki̇ye, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eight-year-old Bodhi from Thailand took the stage at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, to share how his family's durian farm inspired him to think about sustainability and climate change.

As one of nine young participants from six countries, Bodhi delivered a speech titled "A Tree for the Future." Through his family's everyday farming practices, he shared a personal perspective on how small actions can contribute to a more sustainable future.

Since 2019, 51Talk, a global 1-on-1 online English education platform, has helped young participants share their perspectives at UN events. COP31 marks the fifth time the brand has brought children to speak on a UN stage.

From a Family Durian Farm to the Global Stage

For Bodhi, speaking at COP31 was an opportunity to share a story close to his heart. In his speech, Bodhi introduced "2B2P" — Biomass Composting, Biodiversity, Pest Control, and Precision Irrigation — four ideas inspired by how his family cares for their durian farm.

He described how his family turns durian husks into compost to nourish the soil, grows different fruit trees to support biodiversity, manages pests while protecting beneficial insects, and uses water-efficient irrigation methods. Through these examples, Bodhi encouraged people to think about how everyday choices can help protect nature and conserve resources.

"I was a little nervous at first, but my dad told me that my voice matters, too. I wanted to tell everyone about our family farm and make my grandparents proud," Bodhi said.

Having taken English lessons with 51Talk for over a year, Bodhi prepared for COP31 through speaking practice supported by his teachers and family.

Beyond his speech, he also enjoyed meeting children from different countries and learning about their cultures.

"My favorite part was making new friends from different countries! We talked about our favorite things and learned about each other's cultures. It was so much fun that we could all speak English together," Bodhi added.

Building Speaking Confidence Beyond the Classroom51Talk helps children develop practical communication skills through personalized 1-on-1 online English lessons, structured curricula, and a global network of over 10,000 English teachers supported by professional training and teaching standards.

Through interactive lessons and individualized guidance, children have opportunities to practice speaking, express their opinions, and develop confidence in real-world communication.

Bodhi's COP31 experience demonstrates how English can help children share personal stories, connect across cultures, and participate in meaningful global conversations.

"Bodhi's experience at COP31 reflects what we hope more children in Thailand can achieve: the confidence to express themselves, connect with different cultures, and share their ideas with the world," said Emily Li, General Manager of 51Talk Thailand.

Global Communicator Curriculum Planned for Thailand in January 2027Building on its focus on practical communication, 51Talk plans to introduce Global Communicator, its new English curriculum, in Thailand in January 2027.

Based on a syllabus licensed by Oxford University Press and developed by 51Talk, Global Communicator features real-world, cross-cultural scenarios and immersive, task-based activities that encourage children to express opinions, solve problems, and communicate confidently.

AI-supported personalization and learning feedback help address individual learning needs and make progress more visible to families.

About 51TalkFounded in 2011, 51Talk is a global online 1-on-1 English education platform for children aged 3 to 15. Through interactive lessons, structured curricula, and personalized instruction, 51Talk helps young learners build practical communication skills and speaking confidence.

For more information, visit: https://th.51talk.com

data.title: The search for Vietnam's stolen pets at wet markets and slaughterhouses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Scores of suspects arrested this year for stealing thousands of pets
  • Police say stolen dogs and cats are usually sold into the meat trade
  • Vietnam has a long history of eating the animals, but consumption is declining
  • Younger Vietnamese in particular view dogs and cats as companions

By Khanh Vu, Phuong Nguyen and Francesco Guarascio

At a roadside market on Hanoi's outskirts, Kieu Minh Phuong searches for his missing 9-year-old calico among dozens of cages crammed with animals — cats, dogs, rabbits, fighting roosters — destined for anything from sale as pets to slaughter for meat.

Phuong is here because he's seen many stories in Facebook groups of owners finding missing pets at markets like this one.

"There is a high chance that Dom was stolen," the 40-year-old ceramics trader says of the cat he raised from a kitten.

She has never gone missing before, he says, and several neighbours also lost pets the same night.

PET THEFT RINGS

Vietnamese police report detaining scores of suspected pet thieves this year, accused of stealing thousands of cats and dogs to sell for slaughter.

The crime is theft of property. The trade, sale and consumption of cat and dog meat are legal in Vietnam.

There is no nationwide database, but authorities sometimes publish accounts in police-run newspapers. Last month, Ho Chi Minh City police arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats destined for the meat trade. In April, Hanoi police arrested five people over the theft of more than 300 cats.

Criminals tend to operate late at night, riding on motorcycles and carrying sacks, duct tape and makeshift weapons, including improvised stun guns, to subdue the animals, according to the reports.

Hanoi police did not respond to a Reuters request for comment and data on pet thefts.

CLASH OF CULTURES

The criminals are operating at the nexus of a cultural shift in the country of 100 million people, drawn largely along generational lines.

Younger Vietnamese increasingly view dogs and cats as pets, and Hanoi's municipal government has made efforts to curb the trade in dog and cat meat to align with global norms.

However, the meat remains on menus around the country, and whole roasted dogs can be seen in street stalls in parts of the capital.

Rising pet ownership has provided thieves with more targets, which can be sold into a well-established meat trade.

Prices vary widely, but a live dog fetches around $1.50 per kg (68 cents per pound), while a cat goes for closer to $5 per kg, according to the police reports. For context, minimum wage in Vietnam ranges from 69 cents to 99 cents per hour.

"Cat meat is a favourite dish for working-class people," said Tran Thanh, a 50-year-old truck driver from Haiphong.

"Mostly people of my age or older keep the habit," he said, explaining that for about $23 a group of half a dozen people can share a cat-meat hot pot. "We choose cat meat instead of pork or chicken because it goes well with rice wine."

Eating dog and cat meat has a long history in Vietnam, with some believing the meat boosts vitality or wards off bad luck.

There are no official figures on the size of the market, but animal welfare group Four Paws International in a 2020 report estimated that over 5 million dogs and 1 million cats were slaughtered annually.

However, shifting attitudes have taken a toll on the industry, which has witnessed a steady, years-long decline.

"Young people nowadays keep dogs indoors and treat them like members of the family," said Tran Huu Thanh, a 70-year-old former dog meat restaurant owner, who shut his business in 2019 after sales dropped significantly.

Hanoi's government in 2018 urged residents to stop eating the meat, saying it tarnishes the city's image and facilitates the spread of rabies.

Last year, it launched a pilot programme aimed at encouraging dog and cat meat traders to move into other professions by providing vocational training. The finance ministry-run Vietnam Investment Review reported this week that a year into the initiative, 28 businesses had made the switch.

OPEN-AIR TRADE

By law, vendors are required to show proof of origin for the animals they sell, but Hanoi locals say enforcement is lax. Three of the five stall operators at a wet market in the city approached by Reuters said they did not know where their animals came from. All declined to give their names.

The Hanoi city government and the police did not reply to Reuters requests for comment.

Hanoi's largest sanctuary for abandoned and stolen pets, SNNC Dog and Cat Rescue Center, sometimes gets phone calls from people about animals being transported to slaughterhouses.

Workers will often intervene to buy them for more money than their meat will fetch, said Phan Trung Thanh, who volunteers as communications manager for the non-profit group.

But he said SNNC has had to cut back on the number of rescues because it lacks the funds to take in more than the roughly 1,400 animals already at the sanctuary.

Meanwhile, Phuong still has not found his cat, a month after she went missing.

He continues to monitor internet sites where he says people post photos of animals, seeking payment for their return.

"Dom was my emotional support," he said. "The house is empty without her."

($1 = 25,753 dong)

data.title: Australian shares set for best week since August as financials, WiseTech rally
data.description:
Australian shares edged higher on Friday and were on track for their best week since early August, buoyed by financials and WiseTech Global after the software firm reaffirmed its annual revenue targets.

The S&P/ASX 200 index was up 0.4% at 8,796.2 points, as of 2320 GMT. The benchmark has gained 2.4% so far this week, slowly recovering from a 5% decline last week, its worst showing since June 2022.

Sector heavyweight WiseTech Global drove technology stocks 3% higher, with its shares soaring 20% after the CFO voiced confidence in meeting its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast, putting the stock on course for its strongest session in more than two years.

Financials gained 0.5% and were set for a 1.1% weekly rise. National Australia Bank and ANZ Group were the only "Big Four" banks in positive territory.

Energy stocks gained roughly 1% as crude prices settled firmer after mine strikes and an attack on a refinery reignited concerns about global supply disruptions.

Shares of Woodside Energy climbed as much as 2.1% to their strongest level since early November.

Limiting gains, miners fell 0.4% but were set for a weekly gain of about 5%, as investors hunted for bargains after a nearly 13% slide last week.

Bellwether stocks BHP and Rio Tinto fell more than 1% each.

Elsewhere, Australia's Parliament passed a scheme requiring LNG exporters to reserve up to 20% of production for the domestic market from 2028, as the government seeks to ease looming gas shortages on the east coast.

This follows the ruling Labor government's decision last week to exempt the state of Western Australia, which accounts for about two-thirds of Australia's LNG exports, from the scheme.

Farther southeast, New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index was roughly flat at 13,988.06 points.

data.title: Blade Resources Closes First Tranche of Private Placement
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Blade Resources Inc.  (FSE: C3M) (the "Company") has closed the first tranche of its non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") announced on October 13, 2026 and upsized on November 16, 2026. For this tranche, the Company issued 20,300,329 units (each, a "Unit"), at a price of $0.30 per Unit, for gross proceeds of $6,090,098.70. Each Unit consists of one common share (each, a "Share") of the Company, and one Share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant is exercisable to acquire an additional Share at a price of $0.40 for a period of thirty-six months following closing of the Offering.

The Company intends to utilize the proceeds of the Offering to continue exploration and development at the Hot Breccia project, located near Hayden, Arizona, and for general working capital purposes.

In connection with closing the first tranche of the Offering, the Company paid finders' fees of $123,187.90 and issued 410,626 common share purchase warrants ("Finder Warrants") to certain eligible parties who assisted in introducing subscribers to the Offering. Each Finder Warrant is exercisable to acquire an additional Share at a price of $0.40 for a period of thirty-six months following closing of the Offering.

The securities issued under the Offering, and any Shares that may be issuable on exercise of any such securities, are subject to a statutory hold period expiring four months and one day from the date of issuance of such securities.

Concurrently with the closing of the first tranche of the Offering, the Company issued 542,500 Shares to Prismo Metals Inc. ("Prismo") in partial satisfaction of a top-up right arising under the definitive assignment agreement dated February 12, 2026. The top-up right was triggered by the completion of the Offering and the parties agreed to settle the entitlement through a cash payment of $175,000 and the issuance of 542,500 Shares to Prismo, which settlement constitutes full satisfaction of the top-up right.

Certain directors, officers and insiders of the Company participated in the Offering for an aggregate total of $228,000 in Units. Further, Prismo is an insider of the Company by virtue of holding more than 10% of the Company's Shares. The participation by such insiders is considered a "related-party transaction" within the meaning of Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101"). The Company has relied on exemptions from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements of MI 61-101 contained in 5.5(b) and 5.7(1)(a), respectively, of MI 61-101. The Company did not file a material change report more than 21 days before the expected closing of the Offering as the details of the participation therein by related parties of the Company were not settled until shortly prior to closing the Offering and the Company wished to close on an expedited basis for sound business reasons.

About Blade Resources Inc.

Blade Resources Inc. is a Canadian exploration company focused on the development of the Hot Breccia project, an emerging copper-gold porphyry located near Hayden Arizona, USA. Hot Breccia's 227 unpatented mining claims lay in the heart of the Arizona porphyry copper province, within sight of the Hayden Copper Smelter (Asarco) and Freeport's Christmas Mine. Historic exploration on the property conducted by Bear Creek Mining (then a Kennecott subsidiary), in a venture with Conoco Inc., from 1972 through 1981 discovered substantial porphyry copper skarn mineralization in multiple drill holes and confirmed the presence of a large, mineralized Laramide age porphyry; with the grade and tonnage yet to be determined.

data.title: Privacy coins face diverging fortunes as KuCoin moves to drop Monero
data.description:
Crypto exchange KuCoin said Thursday it will delist Monero on Nov. 30, making it the second major platform this month to drop the privacy coin. Exchange MEXC suspended XMR spot trading and delisted its perpetual futures contracts earlier in November.

KuCoin has already suspended XMR deposits and plans to close withdrawals on Dec. 31. XMR fell 10.5% to $449.98 as of 7:00 p.m. UTC on Thursday. The drop extends a decline from about $625 on Nov. 3.

The delisting comes as the European Union prepares to restrict privacy coins on regulated platforms. Starting July 10, 2027, the bloc’s Anti-Money Laundering Regulation will prohibit financial firms, including crypto asset service providers, from maintaining anonymous accounts or accounts that obscure transactions through “anonymity-enhancing coins,” regardless of whether the privacy features are enabled by default or optional. The regulation does not prohibit individuals from holding privacy coins in self-custody wallets.

Launched in 2014, Monero conceals transaction amounts and the wallet addresses of senders and recipients by default. Unlike Monero, Zcash (ZEC), launched in 2016, allows users to choose between transparent and shielded transactions. Both cryptocurrencies have faced regulatory scrutiny over the past few years, with Binance delisting Monero in 2024 and Kraken ending support for it in the European Economic Area later that year.

Zach Pandl, head of research at Grayscale, which launched the first US spot ZEC exchange-traded fund (ETF) in August, said Zcash is positioned differently from Monero. He told Cointelegraph that the firm’s commitment to Zcash will continue for “many years to come.”

Delistings mount ahead of EU privacy coin restrictions

KuCoin’s delisting of Monero follows a series of similar moves by crypto exchanges amid growing regulatory pressure on privacy coins. Since 2018, when Japan’s Financial Services Agency pressed exchanges to drop anonymity coins, regulators in other jurisdictions, including South Korea and Dubai, have also taken steps to restrict their use or availability.

In Europe, plans to restrict privacy coins emerged as early as 2022, when a leaked draft of an Anti-Money Laundering bill came to light. The EU’s regulation defines “anonymity-enhancing coins” as cryptocurrencies with built-in features that anonymize transaction data “either systematically or optionally,” which could bring cryptocurrencies with opt-in privacy features, such as Zcash, within the scope of the restrictions.

Pandl said that viewing keys allow Zcash holders to disclose transactions “to an auditor or regulator, law enforcement if they need.” He said the feature gives users greater control over who can access their financial information. “That is exactly how the financial system works today. It’s just that it gives the authority to individuals rather than institutions,” he said.

However, whether viewing keys alone can satisfy regulatory requirements remains a point of debate.

Other approaches to privacy are gaining traction among traditional financial institutions looking to use public blockchains. In April, Paris-based digital asset infrastructure provider Dfns partnered with cryptography firm Zama to bring confidential transactions to its more than 400 enterprise clients, including banks, fintechs and custodians. The collaboration uses encryption to conceal transaction amounts and balances on public blockchains while allowing authorized parties to access the information for compliance purposes.

Grayscale says shielding beats obfuscation

Grayscale has offered exposure to ZEC since the launch of its Zcash Trust in 2017, based on the view that transaction privacy would be essential for financial institutions to adopt public blockchains.

Pandl said that as AI has advanced, it has become “much easier to link pseudonymous addresses with offchain information.” Monero, he explained, uses ring signatures that obscure the source of transactions among multiple possible signers, a method Pandl said “may be vulnerable” as AI-powered blockchain analytics improve.

“We believe strongly that Zcash is the stronger tech,” he said, because “it takes a shielding approach rather than an obfuscation approach.” Zcash uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify shielded transactions without publicly revealing sensitive transaction data onchain.

Monero developers, however, are working on an upgrade that would replace ring signatures with a zero-knowledge proof system in a bid to enhance transaction privacy.

“For public blockchain technology to become a mainstream part of the financial system, it absolutely needs a privacy layer,” Pandl said.

ETF conviction despite outflows

Grayscale’s Zcash ETF began trading on NYSE Arca on Aug. 25, following the conversion of its Zcash Trust. While investors seeking to use Zcash’s privacy features would need to hold the cryptocurrency directly, “the ETF can provide the store of value use case of these [privacy] technologies,” Pandl said.

Grayscale’s ETF reached $1 billion in assets under management on Sept. 24, but that figure had fallen to $406 million on Wednesday. Zcash more than tripled in value this year, rising to $1,653 on Sept. 26 from $524 on Jan. 1, according to Token Terminal data. Its price more than doubled in the month following the ETF’s launch but has since fallen back to $770. The cryptocurrency remains up about 50% year to date.

Pandl described Zcash’s price appreciation over the past year as “Bitcoin’s Solana moment,” referring to Solana’s growing market cap and its challenge to Ethereum’s dominance as the “leading smart contract platform.”

“At 1.2% of Bitcoin’s market cap, I would still consider Zcash at a relatively low value,” he said, adding that Grayscale has no price targets for ZEC.
